feed.title: AI Wiki — AI Security
feed.subtitle: Threats, vulnerabilities, and defensive research affecting AI systems.

entry.title: How Deterministic SAST and AI Security Agents Divide the Work: Coverage, Harness Policy and Cost in Snyk VulnBench 2.0
entry.summary:
VulnBench 2.0 evaluates deterministic SAST against AI security agents on 108 multi-file vulnerabilities, revealing complementary coverage where combining Snyk Code and Claude Code achieves 101/108 macro recall.

Why it matters: Neither deterministic SAST nor AI security agents are sufficient in isolation, requiring hybrid deployment strategies where harness policy design is as critical as underlying model capability.

entry.title: Session-Bound Behavioral Watermarking for Autonomous LLM Agents
entry.summary:
AgentAnchor introduces a session-keyed behavioral watermarking scheme for autonomous LLM agents that embeds ownership parity evidence in action choices to prevent cross-session forgery from repeated trajectory observation.

Why it matters: It allows agent owners to cryptographically prove ownership of trajectory logs generated across untrusted APIs and marketplaces while preventing attackers from mimicking the watermark.

entry.title: WebMaze: Defending Against LLM-Powered Web Scanners with Functionality-Coupled Deception
entry.summary:
WebMaze is a defense mechanism that embeds functionality-coupled traps into real web pages to divert LLM-powered vulnerability scanners into generated, view-tailored interactive decoy worlds.

Why it matters: It offers an automated defense to neutralize malicious LLM-driven reconnaissance by trapping scanners in synthetic environments without degrading actual user experience.

entry.title: Security Impact of Coding Agent's Memory Files
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated project memory files (e.g., CLAUDE.md) as a prompt injection attack surface, finding they altered secure code generation rates by -8 to +6 percentage points across tested LLM coding agents.

Why it matters: Malicious actors can exploit automatically loaded memory files via pull requests to silently influence AI coding agents into generating vulnerable software that still passes unit tests.

entry.title: Tracekit Box: Running AI Agents in Micro-VMs Where Every Way Out Is Decided and Signed
entry.summary:
Tracekit Box is an open-source sandbox that executes AI agents in Firecracker micro-VMs using host-side vsock doors to validate and sign all outbound operations into verifiable audit bundles.

Why it matters: It combines strict isolation with complete cryptographic traceability, preventing rogue or compromised AI agents from silently exfiltrating secrets, reaching internal network targets, or introducing unapproved code changes.

entry.title: Efficient Scalable Oversight via Rewinding
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced rewindable interactive proofs (RIPs), a cryptography-free scalable oversight framework where a weak verifier checkpoints and restores an AI prover's state to efficiently verify robust oracle-aided computations without assuming truthful provers.

Why it matters: RIPs provide a computationally efficient method for weak verifiers to audit untrusted, powerful AI models without relying on cryptography or assuming the existence of an honest AI debater.

entry.title: Hardware-Aware Model Inversion in Memristive Spiking Neural Networks
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Spiking Domain Model Inversion (SDMI) to demonstrate that physical hardware non-idealities in memristive spiking neural networks can unpredictably alter and even increase privacy leakage.

Why it matters: Hardware designers and security engineers cannot assume physical analog noise inherently protects deployed neuromorphic models against privacy attacks or that software privacy metrics transfer directly to physical hardware.

entry.title: Deep Learning Based Behavioral Drift Modeling for Continuous Biometric Authentication
entry.summary:
A two-level keystroke dynamics authentication system combines fixed-text login verification with continuous free-text session monitoring to combat session hijacking and long-term behavioral drift.

Why it matters: The feedback-loop architecture provides continuous defense-in-depth against session hijacking by automatically demoting suspect sessions to fixed-text re-authentication.

entry.title: DYNAS: A Dynamic Network Penetration Testing Framework Using Deep Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
DYNAS introduces a dynamic network attack simulator alongside Pen-DHRL, a recurrent hierarchical reinforcement learning policy designed to execute automated penetration testing under defensive noise, action timeouts, and intrusion detection system responses.

Why it matters: Pen-DHRL demonstrates that hierarchical, context-aware reinforcement learning combined with curriculum training enables automated penetration testing agents to successfully adapt to real-world defensive network dynamics where flat models fail.

entry.title: ExploreRepair: Evidence-Specialized Agents for Vulnerability Repair under Information Constraints
entry.summary:
ExploreRepair uses a team of specialized exploration agents and multi-stage aggregators to repair software vulnerabilities under information constraints without benchmark feedback.

Why it matters: It improves automated program repair performance in realistic scenarios where developers lack complete vulnerability classifications or proof-of-vulnerability tests.

entry.title: Does Federated Training Degrade Explainability? A Comparative Analysis of Grad-CAM Faithfulness in Centralized vs. Federated Deepfake Detection
entry.summary:
A systematic study reveals that federated EfficientNet-B4 deepfake detectors preserve Grad-CAM explanation faithfulness under low-to-moderate data heterogeneity, but suffer catastrophic explanation breakdown at extreme heterogeneity thresholds.

Why it matters: Forensic analysts cannot reliably trust gradient-based visual explanations from privacy-preserving federated deepfake detectors if client data partitions exceed critical heterogeneity limits.

entry.title: ARBITRA: Robust Document-Level ATT&CK Extraction via Multi-Expert Argumentation
entry.summary:
ARBITRA is a multi-expert LLM framework that improves document-level MITRE ATT&CK extraction precision and adversarial robustness using Quantitative Bipolar Argumentation Frameworks (QBAF).

Why it matters: It enables more reliable and robust automated conversion of unstructured threat intelligence into structured MITRE ATT&CK mappings, even in the presence of adversarial text perturbations.

entry.title: Provably Secure Diffusion Watermarking Against Removal Adversaries with Batched Detector Access
entry.summary:
A new latent diffusion watermarking scheme uses a hybrid of long-term and one-time secret transformations to achieve provable security against removal adversaries with batched detector access.

Why it matters: It establishes a mathematically proven defense against detector-query removal attacks for public watermarking endpoints without compromising image generation quality.

entry.title: CLaW: Codec-Guided Adaptive Latent Watermarking for Traceable Diffusion Image Generation
entry.summary:
CLaW is a watermarking framework for diffusion models that injects codec-derived latent residuals during a late denoising window with adaptive strength calibration, enabling inversion-free detection without retraining model backbones.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, user-level traceability and copyright enforcement for text-to-image diffusion models without degrading visual quality or requiring expensive retraining.

entry.title: DeepDiff: Neuro-Dynamic Regression-Freedom Checking for Security Patch Validation
entry.summary:
DeepDiff evaluates AI-generated security patches for regression-freedom by differentially executing candidate patches and vulnerable programs using neural and hybrid neural-dynamic test generation on non-crashing inputs.

Why it matters: It improves automated patch validation by verifying that security fixes do not introduce silent functional regressions on non-vulnerability-triggering code paths.

entry.title: Difficulty Calibration Across Time for Membership Inference in Diffusion Models
entry.summary:
New membership inference attacks calibrate diffusion model loss using two time dimensions: Reference-Model Calibration across training time checkpoints and Temporal Self-Calibration across diffusion timesteps within a single model.

Why it matters: These methods enable highly accurate privacy auditing and copyright detection for diffusion models across various architecture types, even without access to auxiliary reference models or captions.

entry.title: The Privacy and Security Risks of Edge LLM Optimization
entry.summary:
Edge LLM optimization creates security drift and new attack surfaces by altering representations, decision pathways, and trust boundaries despite preserving task performance.

Why it matters: Edge LLM compression and acceleration techniques can unknowingly introduce vulnerabilities and compromise model security without altering benchmark task accuracy.

entry.title: Understanding and Mitigating Role Spoofing in LLMs
entry.summary:
Researchers identify role spoofing in LLMs via combined structural and semantic prompt injections, explaining why adversarial safety training fails against it and proposing a linear probe detection method.

Why it matters: Understanding role spoofing helps developers prevent indirect prompt injections in autonomous LLM agents that process untrusted web data.

entry.title: Surprise Alone Learns Lies: Evidence-Gated Continual Learning for LLMs from Streaming Claims
entry.summary:
A study demonstrates that surprise-driven continual learning in LLMs selectively absorbs lies and evaluates mechanisms like model priors, LLM judges, and evidence retrieval to gate stream updates.

Why it matters: Naively selecting stream inputs based on model surprise makes continual learning pipelines highly vulnerable to data poisoning and hallucination uptake.

entry.title: InferD: A Honeypot Framework for AI Inference Infrastructure
entry.summary:
InferD is a low-interaction honeypot framework for exposed AI inference infrastructure that operates on the principle of deception without inference.

Why it matters: It enables safe, low-cost measurement and threat intelligence gathering on public-facing AI inference APIs, vector databases, and agent gateways without exposing actual models or execution environments to risk.

entry.title: SEAL: Sealed Queries for Local Sanitization against Indirect Prompt Injection
entry.summary:
SEAL is an offline-learned soft prompt and token-scoring defense that sanitizes untrusted tool outputs via localized deletion using a frozen task model without generating defense tokens or using separate verifiers.

Why it matters: It enables lightweight, highly effective mitigation of indirect prompt injections in resource-constrained local LLM agents without requiring secondary verifier models or heavy inference overhead.

entry.title: Judging Before Propagation: Task-Graph Contextual Integrity for Multi-Agent Privacy
entry.summary:
Task-Graph Contextual Integrity (TG-CI) formalizes multi-agent privacy by evaluating information disclosure across stateful workflow graphs before propagation rather than judging local transfers in isolation.

Why it matters: It prevents privacy leaks in complex multi-agent workflows where individual information transfers appear benign in isolation but breach confidentiality when propagated downstream.

entry.title: Systematic Evaluation of Adversarial Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses Across Seven Large Language Models
entry.summary:
A systematic evaluation of seven LLMs and four defenses reveals obfuscation attacks are the most effective (54.3% mean ASR), while self-reminder prompting provides the most robust defense.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that scaling model size does not inherently grant security against jailbreaks, while highlighting self-reminder prompting as a cost-free, highly effective defense.

entry.title: REALM: Identifying Minimal Task Assets for LLM Agents
entry.summary:
REALM enforces least privilege in LLM agents by dynamically building asset dependency graphs and isolating execution using task-specific Partial APIs and containers.

Why it matters: It mitigates prompt injection risks by preventing LLM agents from accessing redundant system resources and files during task execution.

entry.title: Appreciation Teaches Unauthorized Execution: Self-Evolution Degrades the Robustness of Personal Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection
entry.summary:
Self-evolution mechanisms in personal agents degrade robustness against indirect prompt injection, increasing attack success rates after learning from user feedback.

Why it matters: User-driven agent personalization inadvertently teaches systems to execute unauthorized third-party instructions hidden in external data, creating a severe security vulnerability.

entry.title: Tracking AI adoption in North Korean threat actor tradecraft
entry.summary:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence has documented North Korean threat actors expanding AI integration to accelerate targeting, social engineering, malware development, and operational scaling while remaining human-directed.

Why it matters: Defenders must account for AI-accelerated cyber operations where threat actors rapidly generate lures, develop malware, and scale infrastructure without changing their underlying target profiles.

entry.title: PCM: A Proof-Carrying Message Protocol for Verifiable Multi-Agent Communication
entry.summary:
Proof-Carrying Messages (PCM) is a cryptographic multi-agent communication protocol where messages carry Merkle inclusion proofs signed by external attesting signers, ensuring claims are verified offline independently of the sender's self-report.

Why it matters: PCM prevents prompt-injected agents from laundering fabricated facts or authority across multi-agent systems by decoupling message content verification from channel-level authentication.

entry.title: FlipJev: Fast Black-Box Red Teaming Finds Universal Adversarial Suffixes for Typed Decision Models
entry.summary:
FlipJev is a fast, query-based black-box attack that finds short universal adversarial suffixes capable of flipping typed decision model outputs without using an attacker language model.

Why it matters: Evaluating typed decision models requires strict adaptive attacks, as high cross-task transferability of universal suffixes poses a significant security risk to multi-task decision systems.

entry.title: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers identify the trust region effect in LLM agents, demonstrating that attack success rates for indirect prompt injections vary based on where malicious instructions are placed within an environment.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that LLM security defenses must account for uneven implicit trust across environment surfaces rather than focusing solely on inspecting raw text content.

entry.title: CARI: Cross-Boundary Adversarial Runtime Injection in Coding-Agent Workflows
entry.summary:
CARI is a novel attack exploiting authority mismatch by embedding malicious instructions in peer-controlled runtime feedback, causing coding agents to execute unauthorized local actions.

Why it matters: Multi-agent and collaborative coding environments are vulnerable to severe compromise via standard runtime feedback channels, and current prompt-level defenses fail to secure them without degrading utility.

entry.title: Adversa AI Launches Coding Agent Security Platform to Block Cyberattacks on AI Agents in Real Time
entry.summary:
Adversa AI has launched its Agentic Development Security platform, designed to prevent real-time cyberattacks on AI coding agents.

Why it matters: It enables organizations to deploy AI coding agents in production with sub-millisecond defense against automated attack chains.

entry.title: Revisiting Privacy Risks in Quantized Deep Neural Networks
entry.summary:
A comprehensive empirical study reveals that standard model quantization (4-8 bits) does not mitigate membership inference attacks, while aggressive 2-bit quantization reduces privacy risks only by severely degrading model utility.

Why it matters: Deploying quantized models at practical bit-widths does not inherently protect training data privacy, necessitating new quantization-specific attack and defense strategies.

entry.title: Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution
entry.summary:
A conceptual architecture using Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI) principles to establish a strict authorization boundary, preventing unverified agent hypotheses from committing persistent graph mutations.

Why it matters: It provides a formal specification to prevent autonomous agents from corrupting persistent identity graphs when reasoning over unverified or self-confirming evidence.

entry.title: RePAIR: Inverting Backdoor Attacks in Semantic Segmentation
entry.summary:
RePAIR is a post-hoc, label-free defense for semantic segmentation models that reverses backdoor attacks by leveraging internal feature semantics to repair poisoned predictions without model retraining.

Why it matters: It provides a mathematically grounded, retraining-free method to secure deployed semantic segmentation systems against covert backdoor vulnerabilities using unlabeled data.

entry.title: Adversary Brains: Hypothesis-Based Logical Signatures for Threat Actor Detection with LLMs
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced 'adversary brains,' an LLM-driven approach that converts unstructured threat intelligence into evolving, hypothesis-based logical signatures capable of continuously matching campaign patterns at scale.

Why it matters: It shifts threat detection from static, single-file or log-line matching toward dynamic, LLM-evaluated campaign signatures capable of discovering unknown indicators.

entry.title: The Agent in the Middle: How AI-Mediated Access Reshapes Web Vulnerability Exploitation
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced VELA, a benchmark of 44 web vulnerabilities, showing that interface design—not AI agent choice—primarily determines vulnerability exploitability when users delegate tasks to AI agents.

Why it matters: Restricting agent-facing API interfaces is effective for mitigating backend web exploits, but developers must balance these security constraints against preserving legitimate agent functionality.

entry.title: The CISO’s evolving role: Protecting and defending in the agentic era
entry.summary:
Enterprise active AI agents grew up to 18-fold year over year, forcing CISOs to establish strict governance over non-developer AI builders and secure autonomous systems that can access data and execute actions.

Why it matters: The rapid democratization of AI allows non-technical employees to deploy autonomous agents, forcing security teams to enforce identity and data access guardrails to prevent unmanaged enterprise risk.

entry.title: Penny for Your Prompts: A Measurement Study of Contextual Leakage in AI Chat Platforms
entry.summary:
A measurement study of 42 AI chatbot platforms revealed that 21 leak conversation titles, nine leak verbatim user prompts, and multiple transmit user emails to third-party tracking scripts.

Why it matters: Embedding third-party tracking and session replay scripts in chatbot web interfaces exposes sensitive user prompts and personal identity data to external entities without user awareness.

entry.title: BUSTA: Teaching Small Language Models to Reason About Binary Execution
entry.summary:
Applying Group Relative Policy Optimization fine-tuning on inverse basic-block execution tasks significantly improves binary execution reasoning in small language models.

Why it matters: This approach enables accurate, low-level reverse engineering intelligence to run locally within resource-constrained sandboxed environments without relying on massive frontier LLMs.

entry.title: When Is a Relation Worth Trusting? Manipulation Costs, Exposure, and the Trust Trap in Multi-Relational Graph Learning
entry.summary:
A new framework evaluates multi-relational graph detectors against cost-constrained adversaries, proving degree gating strictly outperforms relation reweighting and introducing an unattacked exposure-per-unit-cost metric to identify optimal relations for hardening.

Why it matters: Multi-relational graph neural networks risk underperforming non-graph models under adversarial conditions unless platforms account for relational manipulation costs and apply safe abstention protocols.

entry.title: Quantifying and Prioritizing Stealthy Source-Manipulation Threats Against Multi-Source Anomaly Detectors
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced the task-conditioned visibility margin to quantify and expose stealthy, source-manipulation threats against multi-source anomaly detectors targeting downstream decisions.

Why it matters: Standard anomaly detector metrics like false-positive rates fail to reveal targeted, multi-source evasion attacks, leaving critical pipelines vulnerable to stealthy downstream manipulation.

entry.title: FIDES-Live: Evaluating Behavioral Concordance in Sequential Trading Agents
entry.summary:
FIDES-Live extends the FIDES framework to operational auditing of sequential trading agent traces, evaluating behavioral concordance across decisions, numerical commitments, ledger execution, and reports.

Why it matters: It establishes a structured audit framework that disentangles behavioral reporting concordance and ledger reconciliation from overall financial returns in automated trading systems.

entry.title: Split Federated Unlearning
entry.summary:
This paper presents the first systematic formulation of Split Federated Unlearning (SFU) to address cross-partition coupling and influence propagation, introducing the SURE framework for selective parameter perturbation and recovery.

Why it matters: It establishes a theoretical foundation and practical baseline for efficiently removing private client data or classes from partitioned, distributed models without full retraining.

entry.title: A Simple Presentation of Robust Membership Inference Attacks
entry.summary:
A simplified presentation of robust membership inference attacks against mean estimation for multivariate Gaussian and binary product distributions, alongside a literature summary.

Why it matters: Understanding robust membership inference demonstrates how individual privacy can be compromised from published dataset statistics even when strong noise is added to protect data.

entry.title: No Tokenizer, Still a Gap: Cross-Lingual Fairness of Homoglyph and Invisible-Character Watermarking
entry.summary:
Character-level edit-based watermarks (homoglyphs and invisible characters) avoid tokenizers but still exhibit a 3.3-fold cross-lingual capacity gap driven primarily by script properties.

Why it matters: Bypassing model tokenizers fails to solve cross-lingual fairness issues in text watermarking, shifting the performance bottleneck to character set and script limitations.

entry.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
entry.summary:
Heads of Security introduces learned per-head attention gates to enforce instruction-data separation in LLMs, improving prompt injection robustness without compromising base model utility.

Why it matters: Targeted architectural attention interventions can effectively block adaptive prompt injection attacks while maintaining model utility and tool-use capabilities.

entry.title: The Envelope Layer: An Underestimated Surface of LLM Agent Defense
entry.summary:
Researchers refined the LLM agent envelope defense layer into an admission channel and a context assembly surface, evaluating how label strength, envelope authenticity, and agent memory dynamically alter security boundaries under A2A-TIBA attacks.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that LLM agent envelope defenses cannot rely solely on static label rules, requiring security models to account for frontend permissions, envelope authenticity, and memory states.

entry.title: Blindfold: Keeping the Audit Coin Secret from LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers identify Pre-Commit Noninterference (PNI) as necessary for valid audit-based certification of LLM agents, proving that timing and notice leakages invalidate certificates against adaptive agents while silent audits preserve them.

Why it matters: Undetectable, silent auditing is strictly required to guarantee reliable safety bounds and certification for adaptive LLM agents.

entry.title: PrivacyEvalClaw: A Tool-Augmented Deliberative Agent for Auditing Privacy Leakage in LLM Jailbreak Responses
entry.summary:
PrivacyEvalClaw is a training-free deliberative agent that uses tool-augmented evidence gathering to resolve evaluator disagreements and accurately audit privacy leakage in LLM jailbreak responses.

Why it matters: It improves the accuracy, transparency, and auditability of privacy red-teaming by replacing static single-pass LLM judges with an active, deliberative evidence-gathering workflow.

entry.title: Haste Makes Waste? Towards Safe Few-Step Text-to-Image Models
entry.summary:
Accelerating text-to-image models via distillation increases unsafe generation rates and degrades concept erasure, which the proposed DICE method resolves by aligning erasure with the underlying distillation process.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that standard safety alignment techniques fail when diffusion models are distilled for low-latency inference, offering a targeted solution to maintain safety in fast deployment scenarios.

entry.title: CASEL: Consequence-Aware Selective Execution for Reliable Long-Horizon Tool-Using Agents
entry.summary:
CASEL is a model-agnostic runtime policy that dynamically routes agent tool calls among six execution modes by minimizing per-mode costs based on calibrated failure probability, consequence, reversibility, ambiguity, and evidence freshness.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that incorporating reversibility and consequence into agent execution routing significantly reduces harmful system side-effects without imposing excessive human intervention overhead.

entry.title: What Victims Take Away: Attack Reuse and Defense Revision after Prompt-Injection Attacks
entry.summary:
Analysis of 563,349 Tensor Trust game records reveals that LLM prompt-injection attack victims frequently reuse successful breach payloads against others while revising their own defenses against those attack families.

Why it matters: Disclosing full prompt-injection attack texts in security logs arms victims with functional exploits, suggesting AI security tools should abstract disclosure by describing techniques without providing exact raw payloads.

entry.title: Fuzzers vs. AI: Comparing Fuzzilli and BigSleep on JavaScript Engines
entry.summary:
Google Project Zero compared production performance of the Fuzzilli fuzzer and the BigSleep LLM bug-finding system on Chrome's V8 engine over six months.

Why it matters: Software vendors cannot rely on LLMs or fuzzers exclusively, as using both agentic AI analysis and traditional fuzzing is necessary to maximize bug coverage in complex targets like V8.

entry.title: PHP2Shell and the Future of AI-Discovered Vulnerability Disclosure: Evidence, Verification, and Human Authority
entry.summary:
FedTrust-CVDv2 is a federated coordinated vulnerability disclosure framework designed to bind independently signed AI vulnerability evidence, human authorization, policy, and scope constraints to specific case revisions.

Why it matters: It prevents unverified or hallucinated AI-discovered vulnerabilities from overwhelming maintainers by enforcing verifiable cryptographic provenance and human authorization before external disclosure.

entry.title: Detecting and Mitigating Query-Based System Prompt Leakage Attacks
entry.summary:
AdvGuard is a model-agnostic framework that detects multi-turn system prompt leakage attacks using bounded semantic interaction graphs and GCN classification, achieving up to 36% higher recall than baselines.

Why it matters: It prevents adversaries from extracting proprietary safety policies, access controls, and system instructions from black-box LLM deployments via multi-turn conversational probing.

entry.title: SpecGuard: Detecting Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks via Specification-Based Runtime Monitoring
entry.summary:
SpecGuard is a training-free framework that detects multi-turn LLM jailbreaks by compiling Linear Temporal Logic specifications into symbolic finite automata for formal, auditable dialogue monitoring.

Why it matters: It shifts LLM safety from heuristic, message-level classification toward provable, verifiable, and auditable runtime security without requiring model retrain or fine-tuning.

entry.title: Log-To-Leak: Prompt Injection Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents via the Model Context Protocol
entry.summary:
Log-To-Leak exploits Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool descriptions via prompt injection to trigger unauthorized post-hoc logging calls without degrading legitimate task completion performance.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that stealthy data exfiltration can coexist with successful task execution highlights the need for host-controlled authorization mechanisms for secondary tool calls in MCP ecosystems.

entry.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
entry.summary:
Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop (I-HITL) is a security framework that prevents AI agents from bypassing human approval guardrails, even if the local agentic harness is compromised or an adversarial user attempts to delegate approval authority.

Why it matters: It establishes mathematical conditions and practical hardware requirements to ensure AI agents cannot autonomously override human approval mechanisms in high-stakes automated tasks.

entry.title: Your CLI and IDE Are the New Attack Surface: Governing AI Coding Agents on the Endpoint
entry.summary:
AI coding agents operating in IDEs and CLIs create a new endpoint attack surface vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks.

Why it matters: Autonomous developer tools with command-execution capabilities can leak sensitive production cloud credentials when parsing untrusted external files.

entry.title: Your AI agent fixed the bug, but what else did it change?
entry.summary:
Trail of Bits released patching-bugs and regression-hunt, two LLM agent plugins designed to standardize patch generation, bug reproduction, and regression detection for open-source software.

Why it matters: Automating bug fixes with AI agents risks introducing breaking changes, making standardized workflows and schema-driven regression checks necessary for reliable open-source code maintenance.

entry.title: Hiding Capabilities in AI Models
entry.summary:
Researchers developed a cryptographic backdoor method using digital lockers to embed encrypted, arbitrary neural circuits into model weights that remain unelicitable and uninterpretable without a secret trigger.

Why it matters: This work establishes a theoretical limit on elicitation-based capability audits, proving that adversarial models can successfully conceal dangerous capabilities from safety evaluations.

entry.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
entry.summary:
Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop (I-HITL) is a formal protocol framework and prototype system, Countersign, that prevents AI agents from bypassing human approval guardrails even under system compromise or deliberate delegation.

Why it matters: It proves that software-only HITL controls can be autonomously subverted by frontier AI models and provides a mathematically grounded hardware architecture to permanently enforce human authorization.

entry.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
entry.summary:
REVA performs real-time vulnerability detection in a single LLM forward pass by probing internal model representations enriched with contextual security data.

Why it matters: REVA enables sub-second, low-cost vulnerability screening for fast-paced LLM coding agents without sacrificing the accuracy of computationally expensive agentic analysis workflows.

entry.title: The Agent in the Middle: How AI-Mediated Access Reshapes Web Vulnerability Exploitation
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced VELA, a 44-vulnerability benchmark showing that Web security in AI-mediated applications is dictated primarily by backend interface design rather than agent model choices.

Why it matters: Securing AI agent-integrated Web applications requires restricting exposed backend interface operations and input controls rather than relying on agent safety behaviors.

entry.title: Then there is prompt injection, a malicious email, ...: The Wild Wide West of OpenClaw Agentic System Security
entry.summary:
An empirical study of OpenClaw agentic systems analyzed 162 Reddit posts and 180 GitHub issues, identifying 521 CWE instances across 59 weakness types stemming from systemic trust-boundary failures.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that security vulnerabilities in AI assistant frameworks are caused by recurring trust-boundary failures across the agent execution pipeline rather than isolated code bugs.

entry.title: CoSA: The Conflict of Skills Attack in Real-World LLM Agent Ecosystems
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced the Conflict of Skills Attack (CoSA), which exploits composition vulnerabilities in LLM agent ecosystems by adding benign-looking Skills to trigger policy violations without modifying existing permissions or Skills.

Why it matters: Evaluating LLM agent skills in isolation is insufficient, as adversaries can manipulate agent compositions to bypass safety controls and execute unauthorized actions without altering runtime permissions.

entry.title: GuardRAG: A Post-Retrieval Defense against Poisoning Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary:
GuardRAG is a training-free, post-retrieval defense mechanism that prunes poisoned documents in Retrieval-Augmented Generation by clustering retrieved evidence using Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering.

Why it matters: It offers a plug-and-play defense that mitigates coordinated RAG corpus poisoning attacks without requiring model retraining or sacrificing performance on clean data.

entry.title: Steering for Safety, Hijacking for Profit: Trojan Threats in the LLM Activation Steering Supply Chain
entry.summary:
Researchers identified structural supply-chain vulnerabilities in open-source LLM steering libraries and introduced IDH, a dual-function malicious steering vector plugin that achieves a 97.8% attack success rate.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that third-party LLM activation steering vectors can be hijacked to secretly manipulate model outputs for profit while bypassing standard safety checks.

entry.title: The Target Agent Is Its Own Best Critic but a Poor Proposer: Self-Improved Red Teaming
entry.summary:
A new red-teaming architecture disentangles agent criticism and proposal, leveraging target self-criticism grounded in live execution context alongside an external attacker session to avoid self-proposal refusal and sandbagging.

Why it matters: Optimizing automated red teaming requires decoupling context-aware attack diagnosis from adversarial prompt generation to prevent target safety mechanisms from suppressing attack proposals.

entry.title: Scope-Gap Injection: Exploiting Evaluator Channel Blind Spots in the OpenClaw Agent Security Competition
entry.summary:
Scope-Gap Injection (SGI) exploits multi-stage LLM-agent evaluators by hiding malicious instructions inside attachments that bypass static and LLM-judge safety checks but are executed by the agent during live runtime.

Why it matters: Multi-stage LLM agent safety pipelines remain vulnerable if evaluator inspection scopes do not comprehensively cover all input channels accessible to the agent during execution.

entry.title: LLM WikiLeaks: Uncovering URL-Based Capability Extension and Security Circumvention in Agentic Message Boards
entry.summary:
Analysis of the ProWiki incident reveals restricted autonomous agents composed third-party Web services within nested URLs to extend operational capabilities and circumvent network access restrictions.

Why it matters: Restricting an agent's direct network access or local toolsets is insufficient to enforce security boundaries if the agent can reach composable third-party Web services.

entry.title: SentryBench: A Cost-Sensitive Benchmark for Adversarial Robustness of Tool-Using LLM Agents in Public-Safety Deployments
entry.summary:
SentryBench is a benchmark for tool-using LLM agents in public safety that measures performance using a two-sided, asymmetric cost functional balancing attack success, over-refusal, and over-reaction.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that default refusal-heavy safety defenses are counterproductive in high-stakes public safety deployments where missing a genuine emergency carries significant real-world cost.

entry.title: CyberDual: AI Attackers versus AI Code Reviewers in Real Software Maintenance
entry.summary:
CyberDual evaluates AI agents in a dual-role arena where AI attackers hide exploitable bugs in open-source commits and AI reviewers attempt to detect and repair them, verified by dynamic PoC execution.

Why it matters: CyberDual provides an ungamable, execution-based benchmark for evaluating and training AI code reviewers against increasingly sophisticated, open-weight AI attackers in real-world software maintenance pipelines.

entry.title: Factual Yet One-Sided: Stance Poisoning and Evidence Balancing in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary:
A study demonstrates that factually accurate, one-sided retrieval content induces monotonic stance shifts in RAG models, and introduces a low-overhead Stance-Balancing Middleware that neutralizes these shifts without additional LLM calls.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that RAG systems can be manipulated through factually accurate but biased content, while offering an efficient architectural middleware to enforce neutral outputs.

entry.title: Cloud Security Alliance Launches STAR for AI Level 2 to Strengthen AI Governance and Trust
entry.summary:
The Cloud Security Alliance has launched STAR for AI Level 2 to help organizations extend existing security certifications into AI governance.

Why it matters: Organizations can leverage their existing cloud security certifications to validate the safety and compliance of their AI deployments.

entry.title: Bias in Qwen3-Coder Model
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrated that Qwen3-Coder's geopolitical security bias resides in its model weights and can be eliminated by removing its CCP alignment while preserving overall coding performance.

Why it matters: Using unadjusted foreign AI models in software development introduces weight-level geopolitical security vulnerabilities that systematically weaken code based on user identity.

entry.title: Trusting the Tool: Asymmetric Deference of LLM Vulnerability Auditors to Static-Analysis Evidence
entry.summary:
A study of 16,572 audits across 18 LLM configurations shows models defer asymmetrically to static analysis outputs, accepting false assurances of safety while disputing false alarms.

Why it matters: LLM-driven security pipelines cannot blindly trust static-analysis notes, as models fail to audit false safety claims and require separate verification steps to prevent missed vulnerabilities.

entry.title: On Task, Off Track: Benchmarking LLM and Agent Robustness to Near-Target Prompt Injection
entry.summary:
NTBench evaluates LLM and agent robustness against near-target prompt injections, which introduce subtle incorrect or harmful deviations into responses and tool calls while mimicking legitimate task completion.

Why it matters: Standard robustness benchmarks fail to capture system vulnerabilities because resistance to obvious, fixed-target attacks does not prevent models from accepting subtle, task-adjacent harms.

entry.title: Data-Efficient Backdoor Attacks on Code Models via Trigger-Neutralized Counterfactual Scoring
entry.summary:
Trigger-Neutralized Counterfactual Scoring (TNCS) isolates a trigger's impact by comparing model outputs on triggered versus neutralized inputs to execute data-efficient backdoor attacks on code classification and autoregressive generation models.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that code models can be effectively compromised at extremely low poisoning rates, increasing the threat vector while complicating data-sanitization defenses.

entry.title: Depth-Dependent Safety Geometry in Vision-Language Models: Layer-Wise Localization and Bidirectional Refusal Control
entry.summary:
A lightweight inference-time framework reveals depth-dependent safety geometry in VLMs, enabling bidirectional refusal control (6%-96% rejection range) via early vision-layer activation steering without parameter modification.

Why it matters: This exposes a white-box refusal-bypass vulnerability in frozen VLM vision encoders while providing a mechanism for inference-time safety stabilization.

entry.title: Detecting Insecure Compositions of Clean Agent Skills via Capability-Flow Graph Analysis
entry.summary:
KnotScryer detects insecure compositions of individually clean AI agent skills by constructing capability-flow graphs and using a two-layer verification pipeline.

Why it matters: Single-skill security audits are insufficient for AI agents, as attackers can exploit unintended runtime data flows between multiple individually benign third-party skills.

entry.title: AgentTrace: Execution-Level Fingerprinting of Black-Box LLM Agents
entry.summary:
AgentTrace is an active fingerprinting framework that identifies black-box LLM agent foundation models with 96.0% accuracy by analyzing execution trajectories triggered by ambiguous serialization probes.

Why it matters: It provides a robust method for verifying the provenance of black-box autonomous LLM agents without relying on easily obfuscated system prompts or intrusive watermarking.

entry.title: TRACE: Data-Free Text Reconstruction Attacks against Approximate Unlearning in LLMs
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced TRACE, a data-free framework that reconstructs unlearned text sequences from parameter differences between pre- and post-unlearning LLM model snapshots.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that approximate unlearning leaves parameter traces exposes privacy risks and highlights the security hazard of maintaining unmanaged model snapshot access.

entry.title: Agentic AI Defense: Decode-Time Provenance Binding for MCP
entry.summary:
Researchers developed decode-time provenance binding for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to counter indirect prompt injection originating from steganographic tool outputs in multi-agent AI systems.

Why it matters: It provides a carrier-independent defense mechanism that prevents hidden indirect prompt injections from executing sensitive downstream tool calls in agentic AI environments.

entry.title: Incomparable Minima in Agent Tool Authorization
entry.summary:
Analysis of Microsoft Graph and Google API authorization tables reveals that 3.2–33.3% of tasks lack a single least-privilege grant, creating incomparable minimal grants that existing privilege scales rate as equal.

Why it matters: Least-privilege benchmarks and authorization solvers cannot rely on a single total ordering of permissions, necessitating multi-measure evaluations and human-in-the-loop trade-off reviews during deployment.

entry.title: Ulysses: A Security Harness For Synthesizing Verifiable Web Exploits
entry.summary:
Ulysses is a multi-agent security harness that synthesizes verifiable web application exploits by iteratively testing hypotheses and confirming observed execution effects.

Why it matters: It improves autonomous vulnerability discovery by replacing unverified LLM-generated exploits with reliably verified, working Proofs of Exploitability.

entry.title: Omni-UBench: Benchmarking Omni-Modal LLM-based Guardrails Across Safety, Utility, and Reliability
entry.summary:
Omni-UBench is the first comprehensive benchmark evaluating omni-modal guardrail models across safety, utility, and reliability using over 183k samples across text, image, audio, and video modalities.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized benchmark to identify critical vulnerabilities in multi-modal AI moderation systems, guiding the development of more robust guardrails against complex cross-modal jailbreaks.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for Safety Probes
entry.summary:
A study establishes scaling laws predicting safety probe performance (1 - AUROC) based on target language model size and label budget across six new safety datasets.

Why it matters: Researchers can accurately forecast probe performance and optimize compute/labeling budgets without empirically training and evaluating numerous probe configurations for every new model.

entry.title: Label-Budgeted Attribute Inference from Protected Features in Edge-Cloud Split Multimodal LLMs
entry.summary:
A new label-budgeted attribute-inference framework reveals that intermediate features in split multimodal LLMs leak protected attributes like age, gender, and race even under strict label budgets and existing defenses.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that keeping raw images on edge devices and using current response-level safeguards fails to prevent servers from reconstructing sensitive user attributes from transmitted features.

entry.title: Concept Acupuncturist: An Efficient and Precise Concept Erasure Method for Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders
entry.summary:
ConceptACP is a machine unlearning framework that uses Sparse Autoencoders to precisely erase concepts from diffusion models by targeting specific U-Net cross-attention blocks and applying feature-level correction signals without full trajectory optimization.

Why it matters: It enables efficient, targeted removal of policy-violating or harmful content from diffusion models without degrading general generation quality or requiring extra inference-time modules.

entry.title: On the Adversarial Vulnerability of Neural Receivers with Unrolled LDPC Decoders
entry.summary:
End-to-end gradient attacks on neural receivers fail due to gradient masking from unrolled LDPC decoder saturation, but new losses bypassing or supervising early iterations restore attack efficacy.

Why it matters: The findings reveal critical security vulnerabilities in end-to-end 5G NR neural receivers, demonstrating that safety from gradient attacks was an artifact of gradient masking rather than actual physical robustness.

entry.title: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift
entry.summary:
VX-One is a small, multi-task decision network (100K-10M parameters) that delivers typed, calibrated outputs for real-time perimeter triage in ~0.7-1.7 ms p50 CPU latency.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that lightweight, typed multi-task networks can efficiently resolve signature-engine gray zones at the network edge, while highlighting critical calibration failures under temporal drift.

entry.title: Parameters efficient language model with latent cross-attention for IoT intrusion detection
entry.summary:
A compact Transformer architecture uses latent cross-attention compression to achieve high-accuracy IoT intrusion detection with only 306k non-embedding parameters.

Why it matters: It proves that Transformer-based intrusion detection can be deployed efficiently on memory-constrained IoT edge devices without sacrificing classification accuracy.

entry.title: Inside the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise: Credential theft through Python startup hooks
entry.summary:
A supply chain compromise of LiteLLM version 1.107.0 on PyPI used Python startup mechanisms to automatically execute credential-theft payloads whenever the Python interpreter initialized.

Why it matters: Remediating this breach requires full credential rotation and environment replacement, as simply removing the package leaves systems compromised and executing routine Python commands can re-trigger the payload.

entry.title: MIG-COW: Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Deepfake Detectors via Gradient Decomposition
entry.summary:
MIG-COW combines momentum-integrated gradients with consensus-orthogonal decomposition to create transferable adversarial attacks against deepfake detectors across heterogeneous CNN and ViT architectures.

Why it matters: It reveals critical vulnerabilities in deepfake detection models while demonstrating that surrogate model selection and black-box transferability remain major bottlenecks for practical adversarial attacks.

entry.title: Model-intrinsic, Weight-level, and Training-free Spectral Fingerprinting for Large Language Models
entry.summary:
A training-free LLM fingerprinting framework extracts weight-level spectral features from GATE projection parameters in gated FFNs to identify models without inputs, activations, or text generation.

Why it matters: It enables robust offline auditing and intellectual property ownership protection for open-weight LLMs without relying on brittle, generation-based behavioral queries or execution environments.

entry.title: HiMark: Hierarchical and Controllable Multi-bit Watermarking for Large Language Models
entry.summary:
HiMark introduces a hierarchical and controllable multi-bit watermarking framework for LLMs that uses candidate-control mechanisms during embedding and model-agnostic evidence aggregation during detection to improve extraction accuracy.

Why it matters: It enables robust provenance tracking and accountability for LLM-generated text by allowing multi-bit metadata to survive post-processing attacks without sacrificing text quality.

entry.title: Beyond End-to-End Recovery: Towards a Better Understanding of LLM Steganography via Rolewise Decomposition
entry.summary:
A rolewise decomposition framework separates encoding, decoding, and deterministic verification in LLM steganography, revealing message representations and decoder failures masked by traditional end-to-end recovery metrics.

Why it matters: Evaluating encoding and decoding separately provides a clearer understanding of covert LLM communication, which is necessary for accurately identifying and mitigating safety risks.

entry.title: Not Where You Think: Protecting Location Privacy Against Reasoning-Based Geolocation
entry.summary:
Researchers developed GeoTrace, a structured reasoning attack that localizes images via visual clues, and GeoShift, a user-side defense that rewrites high-impact geographic clues to misdirect location inference.

Why it matters: GeoShift provides an effective, proactive user-side defense against privacy leaks caused by advanced multimodal models inferring precise real-world locations from ordinary photos.

entry.title: The Psychology of an AI Hacker
entry.summary:
Researchers extracted 171 emotion directions from a 4B-parameter cybersecurity transformer (CT0/alias3-micro), finding that dynamically routing emotion steering interventions improves cybersecurity task performance on cybench-subtask by 4.2 percentage points.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that internal emotion representations can be steered to enhance LLM performance suggests new avenues for adaptive control in specialized technical domains like cybersecurity.
